title: ANIME WORKOUTS - Can you look like Baki Hanma in real life?
summary: NH analyzes early Baki Hanma's physique and writes his own original Baki programs: a calisthenics-only track (5 days, then an advanced 4-day version) and a barbell track (3-day full body, then a higher-volume version). He stresses realistic expectations, age 16+, years of consistency and loving training.
claims: Lifting motivation comes from realism (real legends, athletes) or fiction (manga, mythology); he draws mainly from fiction
He only discusses Baki's pre-Yasha-ape physique, the most achievable version; later versions may be unachievable for naturals
Striving to look like fictional physiques at all costs can harm physical and mental health; he includes disclaimers for young viewers
Follow this routine only at 16 or older
Building a physique takes years, not two weeks
Copying anime characters' routines verbatim gets you hurt or yields zero gains; he writes his own rewrite
Baki's strong points: quads, abs, upper back (mid and lower traps) and shoulders; weak points relative to his frame: triceps, biceps, lats, calves
Dynamic bodyweight movements can be good for hypertrophy if programmed properly
Legs respond very well to barbell compounds and are much harder to grow with bodyweight alone
Calisthenics program minimum equipment: pull-up bar, Olympic rings and resistance bands
Barbell program needs only a squat rack, barbell and plates plus the calisthenics gear; no machines or dumbbells
Learning to program is a big part of building a muscular body; the progression versions teach it
Calisthenics level 1: 5 days a week, mostly AMRAP sets, because unweighted movements recover fast and carry low injury risk
Ring rows are a very underrated upper back movement and solve the difficulty of training the back with bodyweight
Band good mornings tend to be harder than band squats; big quads are very hard to build with bodyweight
Beginner movements are repeated often because they need lots of practice
Advanced calisthenics shrinks to 4 days with more volume per day to build work capacity, adds ring push-ups, weighted pull-ups (3-5 reps x3), pistol squats and harder supersets
The advanced calisthenics program can be run for years and will build a good muscular body
Weight program level 1: 3-day full body built around compound patterns; any knee flexion or hip hinge can replace squats and deadlifts
Deadlifts are left unsupersetted because they need full mental focus; squats and bench are supersetted with band shrugs only because Baki needs lots of trap work
Infinity-set finishers: keep cycling with no rest until it stops being productive, usually 3-4 rounds
Neck development matters if you want to look like a Baki character; they all have massive necks
Lower squat and deadlift frequency than a novice program trades fast progress for patience, better overall development and avoiding plateaus
Loving training is the most important thing; the best way to get big as a natural is sticking to it for a very long time
Full-body 3 times a week has a very good fatigue-to-hypertrophy ratio, though he personally does not like that style
Advanced weight sessions run over 2 hours; to build a big natural body you cannot just train an hour a day
You probably will not look exactly like Baki because frame, insertions and hormones differ, but emulating a character can drive you to your best self
exercises: legs without weights; good mornings harder
